subject: Nexara metrics access and latency exception request
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@nexarahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nexarahealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: SLO / observability questionnaire for procurement review

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for speaking with our evaluation team last week. As part of our procurement review we have a short questionnaire focused on SLOs, monitoring, and customer access to metrics. Our legal and platform teams need to understand how you measure uptime and latency, what alerting is available, and whether Nexara can get read-only access to dashboards during onboarding and post-go-live.

Attached is our questionnaire (nexara-slo-questionnaire.xlsx). High-level items we need answers for:
- How do you define availability and latency at the API level? (per-region / global aggregation)
- Measurement window and aggregator (rolling window, calendar day, percentile definitions)
- What alerting thresholds and escalation paths exist? Can we get alerts integrated into our PagerDuty?
- What dashboards / level of access can the customer have (per-route breakdown, token-level cost, raw logs?)
- Retention for metrics, traces, and request/response logs
- Any exceptions to published SLOs and process to request exceptions

We are on a tight timeline to finalize procurement by end of month. Could you provide a technical point-by-point and any example dashboards by EOD next Friday (Feb 20)?

Appreciate it,
Samantha Lowe
Head of Platform Procurement
Nexara Health

--
Attachment: nexara-slo-questionnaire.xlsx (Excel workbook, 12 KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@nexarahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO / observability questionnaire for procurement review

Hi Samantha — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear list. I attached a short metrics summary (redwood-metrics-summary.pdf) that addresses many of these items at a high level.

Quick answers up front:
- Availability: defined as successful 2xx responses from the public API endpoint, measured per-region and aggregated globally. We exclude scheduled maintenance windows and operator-initiated failovers from availability calculations.
- Latency: measured on request/response round-trip time at the token generation call; we publish p50/p95/p99 per-route and per-region.
- Measurement window: primary SLOs use a 30-day rolling window; alerting uses shorter evaluation windows (5m/1h) for operational triggers.
- Dashboards: we can provide read-only Grafana links scoped to aggregated metrics and per-route latency/availability. We do not expose raw customer PII or token-level request payloads in the shared dashboard.
- Retention: metrics and traces retained 90 days by default; request logs (request ids, timestamps, status codes) retained 30 days. Extended retention can be arranged under a private deployment/enterprise add-on.
- Exceptions: we have a documented exception process (requires internal review, proposed mitigation, and temporary SLO amendment).

Two clarifying questions so we can give the right artifacts: 1) Do you need per-model token-level breakdowns or is per-route sufficient? 2) Are you expecting direct PagerDuty integration for customer alerts or webhook notifications to your monitoring team?

If you prefer, we can also offer a short canary SLO (temporary lower threshold) during onboarding with explicit rollback conditions — I'll loop in Karthik and Lauren internally to confirm feasibility for your tier.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Sales (Redwood Inference)

--
Attachment: redwood-metrics-summary.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

Subject: Fwd: Nexara metrics questionnaire — potential latency exception ask

Folks — forwarding the Nexara questionnaire. They asked for very tight latency guarantees across all regions (they called out 99.99% p95 < 200ms globally). Given their profile (healthcare integrations, bursty inference patterns during business hours) I wanted to check whether we should offer: 1) a documented temporary exception path (e.g., 30-day canary at 99.5% with weekly reviews), 2) scoped dashboard access (read-only Grafana link at per-route aggregation level), and 3) a credit-based remediation if we miss the temporary SLO.

Proposed mitigation plan (draft):
- Canary SLO: 99.5% p95 < 250ms for 30 days, per-region evaluation with global aggregation reported to Nexara
- Instrumentation: enable request sampling at 1% for full traces during onboarding to help diagnostics (not exposed to customer)
- Fallback: automatic routing to a slightly smaller model variant if p95 > threshold for more than 10m
- Credits: 5% service credit per rolling week of missed SLO up to a 20% cap during the canary

I want to make sure this is safe for our capacity plans and that the legal/procurement ask is covered. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Vivek

[Forwarded with original questionnaire attached]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexara metrics questionnaire — potential latency exception ask

Vivek — this is reasonable. I agree with a temporary, documented exception rather than committing to 99.99% p95 globally out of the gate. A few operational constraints to include in any customer-facing doc:

- Canary should be per-region and have an explicit traffic cap (e.g., 10k QPS cap per region during the canary) so we don't oversubscribe nodes unexpectedly.
- Monitoring: we can provide a read-only Grafana dashboard but only aggregate percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and error-rate by route; we won't provide raw request payloads or token-level logs in that view.
- Alerting: offer webhook to Nexara's monitoring endpoint and optional PagerDuty integration (requires a signed contract amendment for on-call routing).
- Auditability: we'll provide the measurement query and the raw aggregated time series used for SLO calcs for audit (CSV export) — not raw logs.
- Credits: OK to offer a limited credit schedule during canary; legal can sign off on standard remediation language.

If Lauren is good with traffic caps and the wording, we can propose the plan back to Nexara. I'll loop legal once they sign off.

—Karthik

Hi Samantha — apologies for the short wait. Per our internal review we can provide the following as part of onboarding and the procurement package:

1) How we measure
- Availability: percent of API calls returning 2xx per-region, aggregated globally. We exclude scheduled maintenance and emergency operator-initiated maintenance windows from the SLO calculation.
- Latency: measured at the API surface for token-generation calls; we surface p50/p95/p99 percentiles computed from the 30-day rolling window. Operational alerting evaluates shorter windows (5-minute and 1-hour) for rapid detection.
- Measurement artifacts: we will provide the exact PromQL (or equivalent query) used to compute the SLOs and a CSV export of the aggregated time series for audit.

2) Monitoring and alerting
- We will give a read-only Grafana link scoped to per-route aggregated percentiles and error rates (no raw payloads). That view includes per-region breakdowns and historical series at 1m granularity.
- Alerting: we can deliver webhook alerts to your monitoring stack and optional PagerDuty integration (technical integration requires a contract amendment to authorize routing).

3) Dashboard and customer access
- Read-only dashboards (Grafana) limited to aggregated metrics. If you need deeper telemetry (traces / sampled request IDs) we can enable 1% sampling for a fixed onboarding period and produce zipped traces for diagnostic purposes — these are not exposed via the read-only link.

4) Retention
- Metrics/traces: default 90 days.
- Aggregated SLO time-series for audit export: 365 days on request (enterprise add-on).

5) Exception / canary proposal (recommended for initial go-live)
- Temporary Canary SLO: 99.5% p95 < 250ms, evaluated per-region, 30-day rolling window.
- Traffic cap during canary: up to 10k QPS per region (negotiable).
- Fallback: automatic routing to a smaller model variant if sustained p95 breach > 10 minutes.
- Credits: 5% service credit per week of missed Canary SLO, up to 20% cap during the canary period.
- Audit: we will provide the SLO computation query plus CSV exports of aggregated series for your audit team.

If that approach is acceptable I can circulate a one-page amendment and a sample read-only Grafana link. For transparency, here are the artifacts I've attached: redwood-metrics-summary.pdf and a short proposed canary runbook (proposed-canary-plan.md).

Let me know if you want the Grafana link active for a short demo next week — we can also walk through the PromQL used to compute p95 if your engineering team prefers.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
